references.text: Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple, right among them. Here too, Jesus escapes a hostile crowd in a miraculous way.
Jesus escaped from the hands of those who wanted to seize him, similar to the miraculous escape in Luke 4:30.
No one laid a hand on Jesus because his hour had not yet come. This shows that Jesus could not be seized until God's appointed time, just as he walked freely through the crowd in Nazareth.
Some wanted to seize Jesus, but no one laid a hand on him. The servants could not explain why they did not arrest him. This illustrates the divine protection Jesus had.
Jesus says that a prophet cannot die outside Jerusalem, which emphasizes that his time to suffer had not yet come in Nazareth.
Fire fell from heaven when soldiers came to seize Elijah. Just as Elijah was protected by God's power, Jesus was also supernaturally preserved from the crowd that wanted to kill him.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego walked unharmed through the fire. In a similar way, Jesus walked unharmed through the hostile crowd – God's miraculous protection of his chosen ones.
The angels brought Lot into the house and struck the crowd outside with blindness. God's supernatural intervention protected Lot from the mob, just as Jesus was protected in Nazareth.
